Here is the report on the winners in the Television categories at the 82nd Golden Globe Awards.

### **82nd Golden Globe Awards – Television Winners Report**
**Date:** January 5, 2025
**Host:** Nikki Glaser

The 82nd Golden Globe Awards honored television productions from 2024. The night was dominated by historical dramas and acclaimed limited series, with *Shōgun* and *Hacks* emerging as the biggest winners in television, each taking home four awards.

#### **Series Wins**

*   **Best Television Series – Drama:** ***Shōgun*** (FX / Hulu)
    *   This sweeping historical drama about feudal Japan dominated the category, beating out heavy hitters like *The Day of the Jackal*, *The Diplomat*, and *Mr. & Mrs. Smith*.
*   **Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** ***Hacks*** (Max)
    *   The comedy-drama starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Jean Smart won this category, defeating nominees such as *Abbott Elementary*, *The Bear*, *Nobody Wants This*, and *Only Murders in the Building*.
*   **Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** ***Baby Reindeer*** (Netflix)
    *   The psychological thriller starring Richard Gadd took the top prize for miniseries. It beat out strong competition including *Disclaimer*, *Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story*, *The Penguin*, *Ripley*, and *True Detective: Night Country*.

#### **Performance Wins**

*   **Best Performance in a Television Series – Drama:**
    *   **Actor:** Hiroyuki Sanada (*Shōgun*) as Lord Yoshii Toranaga
    *   **Actress:** Anna Sawai (*Shōgun*) as Toda Mariko
*   **Best Performance in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy:**
    *   **Actor:** Jeremy Allen White (*The Bear*) as Carmen "Carmy" Berzatto
    *   **Actress:** Jean Smart (*Hacks*) as Deborah Vance
*   **Best Performance in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:**
    *   **Actor:** Colin Farrell (*The Penguin*) as Oswald "Oz" Cobb / The Penguin
    *   **Actress:** Jodie Foster (*True Detective: Night Country*) as Chief Liz Danvers
*   **Best Supporting Actor on Television:**
    *   **Tadanobu Asano** (*Shōgun*) as Kashigi Yabushige
*   **Best Supporting Actress on Television:**
    *   **Jessica Gunning** (*Baby Reindeer*) as Martha Scott
*   **Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television:**
    *   **Ali Wong** (*Ali Wong: Single Lady*) on Netflix

#### **Notable Highlights**
*   ***Shōgun*** secured a historic sweep in the drama category, winning both the top series award and all four acting performance awards within that genre (Lead Actor, Lead Actress, Supporting Actor, and Supporting Actress).
*   ***Hacks*** made history by becoming the first show to win two consecutive Golden Globes for Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy (it also won the previous year).
*   **Ali Wong** made history as the first trans woman to be nominated for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy, though she did not receive a nomination for her stand-up special; however, she won the award for her Netflix special *Single Lady*.

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert ## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). The Brazilian teams qualified were **Palmeiras**, **Flamengo**, **Internacional**, **São Paulo**, **Atlético-MG**, **Santos**, **Fluminense**, and **Juventude**.

Therefore, the five clubs that appear in the qualified lists for all three years are Flamengo, Palmeiras, Corinthians, São Paulo, and Fluminense.

## Medalists in exhibition sports

There are also medalists in [demonstration sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demonstration_sports "Demonstration sports"), or exhibition sports, in which their results are not computed by the IOC for the overall medal table, but the athletes who go to the podium are awarded medals of an identical model to that of the edition, but in a reduced size, with 3/4 of the dimensions of the official medals.

This is the case of [tennis at the 1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_1968_Summer_Olympics "Tennis at the 1968 Summer Olympics"), with the Brazilian [Suzana Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzana_Petersen "Suzana Petersen") who competed in doubles with the Ecuadorian [María Eugenia Guzmán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/María_Eugenia_Guzmán "María Eugenia Guzmán") and with the Soviet, born in Georgia [Teimuraz Kakulia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teimuraz_Kakulia "Teimuraz Kakulia"), winning three bronze medals by finishing in third place in the three modalities (singles, women's doubles and mixed doubles) [[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-petersen-5) and [beach volleyball at the 1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach_volleyball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Beach volleyball at the Summer Olympics"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-volei_praia_1992-6) with the Brazilian men's doubles [Eduardo Garrido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Garrido?action=edit&redlink=1 "Eduardo Garrido (page does not exist)") and [Roberto Moreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Moreira_(volleyball_player)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Roberto Moreira (volleyball player) (page does not exist)"), winning the silver medal[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-7) and [André Lima Perlingeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/André_Lima_Perlingeiro?action=edit&redlink=1 "André Lima Perlingeiro (page does not exist)") and [Guilherme Marques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_Marques "Guilherme Marques") won the bronze medal. In the women's competition, the duo [Roseli Ana Timm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseli_Ana_Timm?action=edit&redlink=1 "Roseli Ana Timm (page does not exist)") and [Rose Barcellos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseliane_dos_Santos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Roseliane dos Santos (page does not exist)") won the bronze medal after beating the duo [Isabel Salgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabel_Salgado "Isabel Salgado") and [Jackie Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Silva "Jackie Silva").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-8)

There was also a specific case with the [Wushu Tournament at the 2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wushu_Tournament_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wushu Tournament at the 2008 Summer Olympics (page does not exist)"), simply called an "affiliated tournament". The inclusion of the martial arts tournament, also known in the West as Kung Fu, in the Olympic program was requested by the Chinese commission. However, the IOC canceled the inclusion of demonstration or exhibition sports after Barcelona 1992, but made an exception for wushu to be contested with its approval, under certain conditions: the fighters had access to all the Games' infrastructure; they could reside in the Olympic Village, use official transportation and credentials, and their fights were reported in official newsletters, including live broadcasts only on Chinese TV; the sport had its own pictogram; Their matches took place in the same gymnasium that hosted the handball tournament, so all the decorations with the inscription "Beijing 2008", hundreds of volunteers, and all the "Olympic-level" facilities were available to those involved. However, the medals distributed were not the official Games model, the athletes could not participate in the opening and closing ceremonies, and there could be no allusion to the terms "demonstration sport" or "exhibition sport" anywhere. Three Brazilians were in the competition and one was a medalist, the fighter [Emerson Nogueira de Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerson_Nogueira_de_Almeida?action=edit&redlink=1 "Emerson Nogueira de Almeida (page does not exist)") won a bronze medal in the sanshou category (up to 85 kg).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-9)

## Special Medals

In 1932, sprinter [Adalberto Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adalberto_Cardoso "Adalberto Cardoso"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-10) was unable to disembark in Los Angeles along with most of the Brazilian athletes and continued to San Francisco with the other members, where he became separated from the rest of the group, disembarked clandestinely and, with 24 hours to go before the competition, traveled the 600km between the two cities on foot and then hitchhiked, only arriving at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum 10 minutes before the start of the 10,000m race. Without having slept for more than 18 hours, without having eaten properly and without time to dress properly, Cardoso competed barefoot and finished in last place, but was applauded by the public and won a special medal of honor in recognition of his effort.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-11)

In 2004, [Vanderlei Cordeiro de Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderlei_Cordeiro_de_Lima "Vanderlei Cordeiro de Lima") was awarded the [Pierre de Coubertin medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_de_Coubertin_medal "Pierre de Coubertin medal"), a rare honor given by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee"). Until that date, it had been awarded only 9 times.
